headline: Review Urban Transit and Trailhead Availability
reservation: Access to Rouge National Urban Park is generally free and does not require a daily entry permit for walking trails. However, specific camping at Glen Rouge Campground requires a separate booking through the Parks Canada system, which often reaches capacity months in advance. Visitors should verify the status of individual trailheads and facility seasonal closures via the official Parks Canada website.

days.title: Wetlands and River Estuaries

stops.name: Rouge Beach and Marsh
stops.detail: Explore the largest remaining wetland in the city where the Rouge River meets Lake Ontario, offering a unique habitat for migratory birds.

stops.name: Glen Eagles Vista
stops.detail: Walk this elevated trail for a panoramic view of the river valley and the geological formations of the Bluffs.

days.driving: Allow 45–60 minutes; conditions vary significantly with GTA traffic
days.note: The beach area can experience high pedestrian volume on summer weekends.

days.title: Glacial Landscapes and Forested Vistas

stops.name: Mast Trail
stops.detail: Hike this historic route used in the 1800s for transporting timber, featuring rare Carolinian forest species.

stops.name: Vista Trail
stops.detail: Visit the two-level viewing platform to see the autumn colors or the dense canopy overlooking the Little Rouge Creek.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes between trailheads; parking is dispersed
days.note: Terrain includes steep ridges; allow extra time for elevation changes.

days.title: Agricultural Heritage and Rural Limits

stops.name: Bob Hunter Memorial Park
stops.detail: Walk through restored tallgrass prairies and wetlands that highlight the region's agricultural restoration efforts.

stops.name: Reesor Pond
stops.detail: Observe waterfowl from the boardwalks in this quiet northern section of the park near the agricultural preserve.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; north-south travel across the park crosses city streets
days.note: Services are limited in the northern reaches; carry water as taps are infrequent.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Parking lots at Zoo Road and Rouge Beach are the first to reach capacity on sunny days. Overflow parking on municipal streets is strictly enforced by local bylaws.

intel.title: Urban Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular reception is generally excellent throughout the park due to its urban proximity. Some deep ravines near the Mast Trail may experience momentary signal drops.

intel.title: City Services
intel.text: Fuel and electric charging are abundant in the surrounding neighborhoods of Scarborough and Pickering. No fueling stations are located within the park boundaries.

intel.title: Commuter Flow
intel.text: Travel times to the park fluctuate heavily based on Toronto highway congestion. Aim to arrive at trailheads before mid-morning to avoid peak transit delays.

intel.title: Public Transit Options
intel.text: The park is accessible via GO Transit and TTC bus routes to specific entry points like Rouge Hill. Check current transit schedules as seasonal shuttles may vary.

plan.arrival: Collect rental at Billy Bishop or Pearson, then stop in Scarborough for supplies before heading to the Glen Rouge area.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are ideal for city streets; check rental terms for driving on unpaved trailhead access roads.
plan.goldenHour: Glen Eagles Vista for sunset, though lighting depends on the season's foliage density.
